product_summary: An AI-assisted compliance platform that turns regulatory requirements into operational workflows, approvals, evidence requests, deadlines, and an auditable system of record.
assumptions: The product is used inside a regulated organization rather than only as a document Q&A tool.
It stores organization-specific evidence, permissions, decisions, and workflow history.
Underlying AI models can be replaced over time.

dimensions.reason: Native model improvements can absorb analysis tasks, but not the organization's governed compliance process and record.
Better models reduce the cost of interpreting documents and increase the product's automation capacity.
AI is important, but the product also owns workflow, permissions, audit state, and integrations.
Evidence, mappings, decision history, and organizational controls compound over time.
The product participates in assignment, approval, remediation, follow-up, and audit.
The interface can be copied quickly, but mature integrations, regulatory mappings, and customer history cannot.
More automated systems increase the need for governance, evidence, control, and auditability.
The model can be treated as a replaceable inference supplier.

why: Core AI capabilities becoming cheaper improves product economics rather than removing the operational need.
The product accumulates organization-specific data, workflow state, permissions, and audit history.
It can become a system of record and control rather than a standalone AI feature.
best_modification: Move deeper into execution by automatically requesting evidence, routing approvals, validating remediation, and preserving complete audit history.
defensive_path: Painkiller → Workflow → Compounding Asset → System of Record / System of Control
decisive_question: If every general model becomes excellent at reading regulations, does the customer still need this system to run, prove, and govern the compliance process?
